item.title: Skyward Group names Apollo CFO as successor
item.description: Taryn McHarg, Apollo’s CFO and Skyward Group’s deputy CFO, will succeed him. Skyward Group CFO Mark Haushill will retire on March 31, 2027, after more than a decade with the specialty insurer. Skyward Specialty acquired UK specialty insurer Apollo in January 2026.

item.title: OpenAI alerta sobre ciberataques de IA: así reaccionan los CISO de América Latina
item.description: OpenAI y más de un centenar de compañías tecnológicas alertaron que los ataques potenciados por IA podrían alcanzar una velocidad y escala capaces de superar las defensas actuales. Regístrate gratis o inicia sesión para leer el artículo completo y descubrir: Perspectivas estratégicas sobre innovación, regulación y tendencias en banca digital y fintech Entrevistas con líderes que están transformando el sector financiero en la región Reportes y estudios que anticipan los cambios clave del mercado Acceso prioritario a información para tomar decisiones informadas y fortalecer tu liderazgo Únete a la comunidad de ejecutivos que marcan la diferencia en la transformación digital de la banca. item.title: Simplicity acquires Wright Wealth
item.description: Simplicity Group has acquired Wright Wealth , an estate and protection planning firm based in Geneva, Illinois. Wright Wealth offers estate planning, life insurance, annuities, long-term care, and wealth protection services to clients in Illinois and across the Midwest. Founder Eric Wright will join Simplicity as a partner and become part of its National Accounts team.

item.title: Bamboo Insurance files for IPO
item.description: Homeowners insurance MGU Bamboo Insurance has filed a registration statement with the SEC for a proposed initial public offering. Bamboo Insurance’s MGA written premium grew from $66.6 million in 2022 to $696.1 million in 2025—a $629.5 million increase, or about 945%. Bamboo describes itself as a technology-enabled, underwriting-first and capital-light MGU that manages data science, underwriting and claims handling while partnering with a diversified group of capacity providers.

item.title: Amica Expands ZestyAI Relationship
item.description: (Image credit: IIR.) Amica Mutual Insurance (Lincoln, R.I.) has expanded its relationship with ZestyAI (San Francisco) by adopting ZORRO Discover, the vendor’s agentic AI platform for regulatory and market intelligence. The expansion extends Amica’s use of ZestyAI technology beyond property risk assessment into regulatory research, competitive benchmarking and filing workflows, according to a ZestyAI statement. Amica first adopted ZestyAI’s Z-FIRE wildfire risk model in 2021.

item.title: Sixfold, PS Advisory Connect AI Underwriting to Salesforce
item.description: (Image credit: IIR.) Sixfold (New York) has formed a strategic relationship with PS Advisory (Baltimore) to embed Sixfold’s AI underwriting intelligence directly into Salesforce workflows. “Our MuleSoft connector links Sixfold and Salesforce directly, giving carriers and MGAs a practical way to bring AI into existing underwriting workflows securely and at scale.” PS Advisory provides Salesforce consulting and integration services for insurance carriers, MGAs, brokers and reinsurers. PS Advisory has built a custom MuleSoft connector that provides bidirectional connectivity between Sixfold and Salesforce, according to a Sixfold statement.

item.title: EV Maker Lucid Recalling 27,000 Luxury Sedans Over Fire Risk
item.description: Electric vehicle maker Lucid is recalling 27,185 of its flagship Air luxury sedans in the U.S., because an exterior lighting circuit could overheat and increase the risk of a fire, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Friday. (Reporting by Sailesh in Bengaluru; Editing by Mrigank Dhaniwala and Devika Syamnath) Get the latest insurance news sent straight to your inbox.

item.title: US Widens Lettuce-Related Cyclosporiasis Probe to 20 States
item.description: health authorities have widened their probe into a cyclosporiasis outbreak tied to iceberg lettuce from central Mexico after detecting cases in three additional states, raising the total to 20 states, the FDA and CDC said on Thursday. The outbreak, linked to iceberg lettuce served at Taco Bell restaurants and sourced from Taylor Farms’ operations in Mexico, has grown to 11,458 cases, including 495 hospitalizations. (Reporting by Santhosh in Bengaluru; Editing by Leroy Leo) Get the latest insurance news sent straight to your inbox.

item.title: Russian-Speaking Cybercriminals Used SpaceX’s AI Tool to Hack Seven Companies
item.description: Russian-speaking hackers used SpaceX’s AI coding assistant, Cursor, to help break in to a Belgian chemical company and at least six other firms earlier this year, according to data reviewed by Reuters and reports issued on Thursday by cybersecurity companies Gambit Security and CloudSek. The cybercriminals’ AI-boosted hacking spree is the latest example of how rogue actors are using commercial AI tools to carry out intrusions. Related: As AI Agents Go Rogue, Cyber Insurers Are Adapting Their Policies Cursor and its parent company, SpaceX, did not return messages seeking comment.

item.title: Meta Joins List of Firms That Settled Cases for Billions of Dollars
item.description: Enron, once the nation’s seventh-largest company, filed for bankruptcy protection in 2001, after years of accounting tricks could no longer hide billions of dollars in debt or make failing ventures appear profitable. In 2005, the company agreed to pay shareholders about $750 million in cash and stock, while major banks and accounting firms settled for about $6 billion. Tech giant Meta this week agreed to pay $17 billion as part of a settlement to end a landmark trial related to safeguards for younger users of social media.

item.title: Major Tech Companies Call for Cyber Defense Priority to Defeat AI-driven Hacks
item.description: Major tech companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon are calling for a society-wide defensive surge to defeat what they describe as an impending wave of hacks driven by artificial intelligence. It called on government and industry leaders “to bring the full weight of their technology, resources, and expertise to this effort.” It called on governments to expedite trusted access programs, which give certain companies access to more powerful models ahead of the general public, and for all other organizations to “make cyber defense an immediate leadership priority.” The U.S. In a joint letter issued Thursday, the companies — along with more than 100 others including Broadcom, Capital One, Cloudflare, CrowdStrike, General Motors, IBM, Mastercard, Oracle, Robinhood, Shopify, and Visa — said there was a limited amount of time “to make our digital world much more secure” ahead of the AI threat.

item.title: Insurance Industry Employee Confidence Tanks on AI Concerns: Report
item.description: Glassdoor’s Employee Confidence Index for its broader AI Report hit a record 10-year low in July, and a large percentage came from the insurance sector. From late 2023 to early 2024, insurance industry employee confidence dropped significantly (in line with a broader decline in employee confidence), but rebounded until May of 2026. A new report highlights insurance industry employees growing negativity toward AI job displacement, as sector employment dropped 21% YoY, and entry-level adjuster positions dropped 50% YoY.

item.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI Tools And Assistants Lead Sparser Lineup Of Megadeals
item.description: Most of this week’s largest funding recipients were AI-focused startups, with Instinct , a developer of AI assistants, pulling in the biggest round. This is a weekly feature that runs down the week’s top 10 announced funding rounds in the U.S. Check out last week’s biggest funding deal roundup here .

item.title: Underwriting discipline and risk transparency key as casualty ILS evolves: AM Best
item.description: As the casualty insurance-linked securities (ILS) market continues to expand, rating agency AM Best has indicated that market participants will need to remain focused on ensuring that both underwriting discipline and risk transparency develop simultaneously in order to keep pace with investor demand. In addition, AM Best emphasised that, in contrast to many catastrophe exposures, the underwriting risks linked to casualty business may not become fully evident for prolonged periods. While innovation in the capital markets can offer significant sources of capacity, AM Best has pointed out that some reinsurers have raised concerns about the speed and framework of specific casualty insurance-linked securities initiatives.

item.title: Aon says ILS has become a source of ‘foundational reinsurance capital’ as growth continues
item.description: The insurance-linked securities (ILS) market grew to $144.5 billion as of the end of June 2026, which re/insurance broking group Aon says represents an annual growth rate of 8.4% over the past five years, ensuring ILS has become a source of “foundational reinsurance capital.” Aon Securities’ 20th and latest ILS market report analyses sector activity during the 12-months ending June 30, 2026. “The past 12 months marked an important milestone for the ILS market as it continued to evolve into a source of foundational reinsurance capital for clients globally. According to Aon, outstanding sidecar capital rose to $23 billion across both property and casualty lines, approximately 50% higher than year-end 2024, driven by both strong margins and growth in casualty-focused sidecars reinsurance vehicles.

item.title: SCOR Business Solutions announces Energy team appointments
item.description: SCOR Business Solutions, the large corporate risk insurance arm of global reinsurer SCOR, has announced a number of appointments across its Energy team. Sim joined SCOR Business Solutions in February 2022 as Senior Energy Underwriter, focusing on strengthening relationships with key clients across the Asia-Pacific region. He has been at SCOR since 2012 and has built extensive international experience across the Energy sector, most recently leading the firm’s Energy business for the Asia-Pacific region from Singapore.

item.title: China Re P&C H1’26 net income falls slightly, Chaucer and overseas P&C premium income up 3%
item.description: In the first half of 2026, China Re also reported total premium income from the overseas P&C reinsurance and Chaucer business of RMB 18,064 million, representing a year-on-year increase of 3%. China Reinsurance (Group) Corporation (China Re) has released its unaudited results for the first half of 2026, reporting net income of RMB 2,313 million from its property and casualty subsidiary, reflecting a slight 1.1% decrease from RMB 2,338 million in the same period last year. (China Re P&C) – offers a wide variety of reinsurance products for various property and casualty insurance, such as motor, property, agricultural and liability insurance, and also includes the business operated by Chaucer.

item.title: First US Phosphate Plant in Decades Planned Amid Global Conflict
item.description: The proposed plant in Waggaman, Louisiana, the first of its kind in the US in over four decades, would produce more than a million tons of phosphate-based fertilizer annually, according to a Wednesday press release. and fertilizer producer OCP North America are proposing a $450 million phosphate fertilizer plant in Louisiana, bolstering domestic supplies as global conflicts have increasingly thwarted the flow of foreign crop nutrients. The announcement comes as global fertilizer markets have been roiled by geopolitical conflict, first in Russia and Ukraine and then in the Middle East.

item.title: Ross Fire Grows Into One of Largest Wildfires on Record in North Texas
item.description: The Ross Fire has grown into one of the largest wildfires in the Dallas-Fort Worth area’s recorded history, scorching 85,000 acres across Palo Pinto and Jack counties in just three days. As much of the state experiences extreme heat, the Forest Service reports 80 active fires scorching over 90,700 acres across Texas, including the Ross Fire. The Ross Fire is now the second-largest wildfire in the area’s history, according to the National Weather Service’s Fort Worth office, behind the Possum Kingdom Complex Fire, which burned 126,734 acres in April 2011.

item.title: New Illinois Law Requires Insurance for High-Speed E-Bikes
item.description: Illinois joins New Jersey as the only states to require insurance for high-seed e-bikes. The new law requires riders of e-bikes and e-motors capable of traveling over 28 mph to have a driver’s license, title, registration and insurance. Illinois Senate Bill 3484 draws a distinction between bicycles, lower-speed e-bikes and higher-powered e-bikes.

item.title: Tokio Marine HCC International to acquire UK MGA Direct Commercial
item.description: Tokio Marine HCC International (TMHCCI), a member of Tokio Marine HCC (TMHCC), has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Direct Commercial (DCL), a specialist UK commercial motor managing general agent, and its sister company, Direct Commercial Premium Finance. DCL is headquartered in Chelmsford, Essex, and is one of the UK market’s “fastest-growing” motor fleet underwriters, providing commercial fleet cover for operators across the UK. The acquisition opens TMHCCI to a new line of business in commercial motor.

item.title: Corgi looks to expand into life and health insurance
item.description: Corgi appears to be expanding beyond property and casualty insurance into life and health products. The insurer is hiring a Life and Health Actuary to build its actuarial function across employee benefits and supplemental insurance. Corgi lists current or recent experience at Aflac , or a comparable supplemental health or benefits carrier, as a preferred qualification.

item.title: The Hartford partners with UC Berkeley’s Bakar Labs For Energy & Materials
item.description: The Hartford is teaming up with UC Berkeley’s Bakar Labs to support startup companies creating next-generation energy and materials technologies. Bottom Line: The Hartford is partnering with UC Berkeley to mentor clean-tech and AI-energy startups, offering them hands-on risk management advice as they scale up. In addition, The Hartford will be the only insurance company joining UC Berkeley’s Launch Advisory Group.

item.title: La IA no es el camino hacia la confianza, señalan bancos colombianos
item.description: La banca colombiana enfrenta el reto de sostener y construir confianza en una época marcada por la inteligencia artificial (IA), decisiones basadas en datos y modelos estadísticos. La concepción del cliente en el centro esta más presente que nunca, pero los líderes creen que el siguiente paso es establecer una banca más conversacional, cercana y empática con los “momentos” del usuario y sus necesidades financieras. item.title: Corgi raises another $40.7 million
item.description: Corgi has completed a $40.7 million securities offering involving equity and rights to acquire additional securities, according to a regulatory filing. The filing follows several previously announced rounds, including a $160 million Series B and a subsequent $106 million raise that valued Corgi at $2.6 billion. Founded in 2024 by Nico Laqua and Emily Yuan, Corgi operates an AI-focused insurance platform serving startups and other commercial businesses.

item.title: New York City Faces Flood Risks From Thunderstorms
item.description: Northeast and Mid-Atlantic, including New York City, face another round of thunderstorms, increasing flood risks and transportation woes, with even the slight chance of a tornado. In addition to the flood threat to nearly 39 million people, there is a level 2 risk of severe thunderstorms bringing hail and damaging winds across a large part of the Mid-Atlantic from Upstate New York to Northern Virginia, the US Storm Prediction Center said. Flood watches will cover New York’s five boroughs, as well as stretching from the lower Hudson Valley across New Jersey to eastern Pennsylvania, including Philadelphia, starting midday Thursday, the National Weather Service said.

item.title: Young investors trust AI more than TV or celebrities
item.description: New research focused on 18- to 40-year-olds who own or are considering investments showed that 56% trust AI tools, more than TV and radio (47%), press (46%) or social media influencers (29%). Four in 5 less experienced investors have used AI for help with investing – and around two-thirds report doing so occasionally or regularly. And people are getting more comfortable, with two-thirds expecting to lean on AI even more over the next year.

item.title: AI-Driven Hacks Shake Up Cyber Insurance Industry
item.description: The rise of artificial intelligence-powered hacks has cyber insurance firms rethinking their policies, Reuters reported Thursday (Aug. However, the hacks still spotlight the changing cyber risks faced by companies and insurers. The global cyber insurance market is expected to reach around $28 billion by 2030, the report said, citing data from Munich Re .

item.title: Craft’s Ilya Levtov Never Learned To Code. He Built A Software Company Anyway.
item.description: Years later, after building Craft , a 12-year-old San Francisco-based supply chain software company that he says now works with 35 federal agencies and generates double-digit millions of dollars in annual recurring revenue, that remains true: “And I still haven’t written a single line of code.” Over the years, Levtov raised $42 million in funding for Craft. “I’ve never written a line of code in my life,” Levtov told Crunchbase News in an interview. By conventional Silicon Valley standards, Ilya Levtov had some of the credentials one might expect of a startup founder: Stanford Business School , experience as a VC on Sand Hill Road, and time working inside a fast-growing venture-backed startup.

item.title: Socure Secures $156M at $5.2B Valuation, Acquires AI Fraud Investigation Startup Fravity
item.description: Identity verification and fraud prevention company Socure announced Thursday that it raised $156 million in a strategic growth investment valuing it at $5.2 billion. The Incline Village, Nevada-based company is also acquiring Austin-based agentic AI startup Fravity as it looks to automate more of the labor-intensive work involved in investigating financial crime. Socure did not disclose the terms of its acquisition of Fravity.

item.title: Brookmont cat bond ETF listing moving to Texas, as it targets lead market maker for fund
item.description: Brookmont Capital Management, LLC, is set to move the listing venue for its Brookmont Catastrophic Bond ETF (ILS) strategy to the Texas Stock Exchange as it hopes to onboard the first lead market maker to the fund within weeks. The Brookmont Catastrophic Bond ETF failed to secure a lead market maker for its launch, in part because the ILS asset class is difficult to hedge, but now the firm behind it is hopeful this move to a Texas Stock Exchange listing may make that a simpler process. Bid–ask spreads remained tight at around 10 basis points on a median basis, reflecting an efficient secondary market and effective support from the ETF’s authorized participants.” Powell of Brookmont further explained that the transfer of the listing to Texas is “an opportunity to continue to grow and scale ILS, facilitated by a lead market maker.”

item.title: Fermat UCITS and offshore catastrophe bond funds each surpass $3bn of assets
item.description: Fermat Capital Management recently hit new milestones for two of its dedicated catastrophe bond fund strategies, taking the pair to more than $3 billion of assets under management each, while achieving those levels of assets at a particularly rapid pace, Artemis can report. With its UCITS cat bond fund hitting the $3 billion of assets level in around two and a half years, the ILS manager Fermat’s offshore cat bond fund strategy has technically achieved the same milestone even faster. As perhaps the largest holder and manager of catastrophe bond portfolios in the world, Fermat Capital Management now actively manages two of the largest cat bond fund strategies on offer, with only a handful of funds ever having reached the $3 billion level.

item.title: Reask study shows how pre-landfall parametric triggers fund pre-storm protective actions
item.description: A new study co-authored by catastrophe modelling and climate analytics specialist Reask, has demonstrated how advanced downstream forecast analytics can eliminate basis risk in parametric insurance by funding pre-landfall protective actions before a hurricane strikes. We put the back-tests in an app so anyone can check the calibration themselves rather than take our word for it.” Importantly, as it’s clearly showcased that LiveCyc can reliably generate 1,000 realisations at 1-km resolution, the study establishes the mathematical foundation required to structure automated pre-landfall parametric insurance triggers. David Schmid, Global Head of Data Products, Reask, commented: “To embed this into a holistic risk management approach, that very same threshold can be used to trigger a pre-landfall payout from a parametric insurance cover, sized to match the cost of the protective action.

item.title: Swiss Re appoints Ludovic Boulanger as Market Head Life & Health France
item.description: Global reinsurer Swiss Re has announced the appointment of Ludovic Boulanger as Market Head Life & Health France. In his new role, Boulanger will be responsible for strengthening Swiss Re’s long-term partnerships with clients and contributing to the development of the Life & Health market in France, combining technical expertise, an understanding of clients’ needs, and reinsurance solutions. Boulanger joins Swiss Re from Arundo Re, where he most recently served as a Life & Health underwriter, responsible for developing its Life & Health portfolio and maintaining strong relationships with existing partners.

item.title: Peak Re sees H1’26 reinsurance revenue increase 25% with net profit reaching $89.7m
item.description: Fosun International Limited has released the unaudited first half of 2026 results for Hong Kong-based global reinsurer Peak Re, reporting a 25.0% year on year increase in reinsurance revenue to USD825.7 million, and an 11.8% rise in gross written premiums to USD1,186.0 million. Profit attributable to owners of the parent reaching RMB1.72 billion, representing a year-on-year increase of 160.3%. Net profit after tax reached USD89.7 million, reflecting solid profitability, with the reinsurance service result remaining stable at USD70.4 million.

item.title: AIG welcomes two new members to its Casualty DACH team
item.description: AIG, a global insurance organisation providing a broad range of commercial insurance and risk management solutions, has welcomed two new colleagues to its Casualty DACH team in Germany. Filip Karbunarevic has joined AIG’s Frankfurt office as Underwriting Analyst Casualty, Northern Germany, becoming part of Team North. AIG welcomes Bianca and Filip to the team and looks forward to continuing the constructive discussions already underway and working together on the opportunities ahead.

item.title: Marketing Firm Sued for Refusing to Hire Pregnant Woman
item.description: International advertising and marketing firm Dentsu International Americas, LLC, violated federal law when it refused to hire a pregnant woman for a Minneapolis-based position promoting alcoholic beverage brands, the U.S. Such conduct violates the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act, which prohibits an employer from refusing to hire a pregnant employee because she will need a reasonable accommodation, which can include time off to recover from childbirth. According to the suit, in November 2023, Dentsu refused to hire a female applicant for a position promoting alcoholic beverage brands and instead hired a less-qualified male applicant.

item.title: Carnival Cruise Line Wins New Trial After $10M Verdict in Sex Assault Suit
item.description: Carnival Cruise Line, long the subject of lawsuits accusing its crew members of unwanted sexual advances on passengers, has won a new trial in a case in which a Florida jury awarded $10.3 million to a young woman who said she was assaulted in 2018. “…We reverse the district court’s grant of partial summary judgment on the false imprisonment claim, vacate in part the judgment of the district court as to the false imprisonment and sexual assault claims, and remand for a new trial on the false imprisonment and sexual assault claims,” the U.S. The appellate judges agreed with Carnival’s argument that the lower federal court in southern Florida erred by not allowing the jury to hear about an FBI report that had concluded that the sexual encounter on the cruise ship was consensual.

item.title: DICEUS partners with Kruzr to power connected motor insurance
item.description: DICEUS has partnered with Kruzr to connect the latter’s smartphone telematics and driver-safety capabilities with the DICEUS insurance platform, helping insurers turn real-world driving behaviour into action. Connected and usage-based insurance continue to reshape motor insurance. DICEUS and Kruzr are partnering to bring those capabilities into one connected environment.

item.title: The Easiest Cross-Sell Opportunity
item.description: Independent agents can cross-sell commercial coverage to personal lines clients using modern quoting technology and relationship advantages. A good management system can flag commercial cross-sell and upsell opportunities directly inside your existing client records. It's an easy opportunity to overlook, though.

item.title: Urban Risk Isn't Uninsurable, It's Misunderstood
item.description: That reality shaped District Cover’s Urban Risk Report . There’s a growing perception that urban risk is becoming harder to insure, and in some ways that’s understandable. Even as pricing softens elsewhere in commercial lines, that relief hasn’t reached urban corridors to the same degree — density means claims are more correlated, and social inflation has hit liability lines especially hard, so urban risk is still being priced against a liability curve that hasn’t softened the way property has.

item.title: How to Manage Pandemic Risk
item.description: Recent outbreaks of Andes hantavirus and Bundibugyo Ebola have renewed attention on pandemic risk, but neither currently appears likely to cause sustained global spread. Recent hantavirus and Ebola outbreaks underscore that pandemic preparedness depends on rapid detection and response systems, not pathogen severity alone. Their main significance lies in what they reveal about pandemic preparedness: the importance of rapid detection, effective contact tracing, international coordination, and timely countermeasures.

item.title: Lockton Performance launches new coverage
item.description: We understand the unique responsibilities that come with buying, selling, storing, transporting and maintaining high-quality vehicles, and we work with our clients to arrange cover that reflects the way they operate.” – John Collyear, Senior Vice President, Lockton Performance. Lockton has launched a Specialist Motor Trade Insurance product designed for UK businesses such as collector car dealers, storage facilities and specialist workshops. The product will deliver up-to-date cover, tailored to the vehicles these businesses handle and the way they operate.

item.title: Arch launches management liability product on Ebix exchange
item.description: Arch Insurance Australia has launched its Management Liability Plus product on Ebix Australia’s Sunrise Exchange. Coverage includes PR and crisis management costs, defamation, privacy infringement, personal cyber liability and social engineering, in addition to standard management liability protections. The digital portal allows brokers serving small and midsize organizations to access coverage options, receive real-time referrals, modify policies midterm and communicate directly with Arch underwriters through LiveChat.

item.title: Hippo to expand homeowners insurance
item.description: Hippo announced that its Hippo Homeowners Insurance Program will expand its availability into 14 additional states through relationships with national distribution partners, increasing the number of states where the program is available from 8 to 22 states in the fourth quarter. Starting in the fourth quarter, the Hippo Homeowners Insurance Program will be available to homeowners beyond the newly built home channel in Alabama, Arkansas, Arizona, Indiana, Michigan, Missouri, Nevada, New Jersey, New York, Oregon, Utah, Virginia, Washington and Wisconsin. We’re now in a position to selectively expand homeowners again.

item.title: PwC International Can’t Exit Evergrande Case, HK Court Rules
item.description: Deputy High Court Judge Patrick Fung said the evidence PwC International submitted as part of its arguments to exit the case was “inadequate and unsatisfactory,” according to a judgment delivered on Wednesday. A Hong Kong court declined to remove PricewaterhouseCoopers International Ltd. The case centers on PwC’s auditing work for Evergrande, an emblem of China’s property crisis since it defaulted in 2021.
